newsitem.title: FRANCE: New system planned for France Telecom sale.
newsitem.headline: New system planned for France Telecom sale.

text.p: France plans to introduce a new system allowing private investors to reserve shares in France Telecom ahead of its official sale on May 27, French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Thursday.
The new system is designed to fuel interest in the sale, which Arthuis described as "the biggest flotation ever carried out in France" and create a culture of popular shareholding.
"The reservation system will be at the heart of the publicity campaign," Arthuis said "The aim is to get as much of the public involved as possible."
The new reservation system -- which will require a modification to a 1993 law -- will allow people to reserve shares at their bank before a firm price is set.
They will then have the right but not the obligation to buy France Telecom shares in the float.
On Wednesday, France Telecom chairman Michel Bon said he hoped to have more than two million shareholders after the float.

France plans to sell between 30 and 50 billion francs in France Telecom shares in a market operation which could raise more money for the government than the February 1994 float of Elf-Aquitaine which raised 35.7 billion francs.
The period for reservation will start on May 6, after a price range will have been set in the evening of May 5, and last until May 26.
The actual market flotation will start on May 27 and close on June 3 with the first share trading in New York and Paris scheduled for June 9.
